Order a metric-definition workflow.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Define the desired outcome"},{"id":"s2","text":"Choose observable measures"},{"id":"s3","text":"Specify how each measure is computed"},{"id":"s4","text":"Set acceptance and guardrail thresholds"},{"id":"s5","text":"Run representative evaluation and compare to thresholds"}]
Metrics become useful only after outcome, measurement, and thresholds are explicit.
Order a basic evaluation-framework design.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Define representative tasks"},{"id":"s2","text":"Choose appropriate graders"},{"id":"s3","text":"Run one or more trials"},{"id":"s4","text":"Collect trajectories/outcomes"},{"id":"s5","text":"Aggregate results against thresholds"}]
Task definition and grading come before execution and aggregation.
Order a controlled improvement experiment.

[{"id":"s1","text":"State the hypothesis"},{"id":"s2","text":"Choose primary and guardrail metrics"},{"id":"s3","text":"Define assignment and decision rule"},{"id":"s4","text":"Run control/treatment or shadow evaluation"},{"id":"s5","text":"Analyze results and decide whether to ship"}]
Pre-specification precedes execution and interpretation.
Order a root-cause diagnostic loop.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Reproduce the symptom"},{"id":"s2","text":"Inspect trace/outcome evidence"},{"id":"s3","text":"Identify the likely failing stage"},{"id":"s4","text":"Run a targeted isolation test"},{"id":"s5","text":"Apply the fix and add regression coverage"}]
Evidence-driven isolation precedes remediation.
Order a safe optimization cycle.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Measure baseline quality, latency, and cost"},{"id":"s2","text":"Identify the dominant resource driver"},{"id":"s3","text":"Apply one targeted optimization"},{"id":"s4","text":"Re-run quality/safety/latency evals"},{"id":"s5","text":"Keep the change only if all required thresholds pass"}]
Optimization remains constrained by outcome quality and safety.
Order a production learning loop.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Monitor real system behavior"},{"id":"s2","text":"Detect and investigate a failure/drift signal"},{"id":"s3","text":"Fix the root cause"},{"id":"s4","text":"Add a regression case"},{"id":"s5","text":"Verify the fix in evaluation and production"}]
Production evidence feeds back into regression protection.
What is the core safety architecture principle for guardrails?
Use defense in depth rather than relying on a single control.
Why are system prompts insufficient as hard security boundaries?
Model behavior is probabilistic and can be influenced by adversarial or unexpected inputs.
Where should a safety or authorization control live?
At the boundary capable of actually enforcing the required property.
What is indirect prompt injection?
Malicious instructions embedded in external content that an agent processes.
What is excessive agency?
Giving an agent more autonomy, tools, permissions, or side-effect power than the task requires.
What three control categories help structure risk treatment?
Prevention, detection, and recovery.
When should human involvement increase?
As consequence, irreversibility, uncertainty, or regulatory obligation increases.
What is pre-action approval?
A human reviews and authorizes a proposed consequential action before execution.
Why is human review ineffective when the reviewer lacks context?
The human cannot make a meaningful decision and may merely rubber-stamp the model.
What is the core architecture task for compliance requirements?
Translate applicable obligations into specific controls, owners, evidence, and review processes.
Why does a provider's compliance status not automatically make an application compliant?
Compliance depends on the full system boundary, data flows, configuration, controls, and organizational responsibilities.
Why can aggregate accuracy hide fairness problems?
Different relevant populations or use cases may experience materially different error rates.
What does accountability require in AI architecture?
Named human/organizational ownership for decisions, residual risk, monitoring, incidents, and policy changes.
Defense in depth
Using multiple independent layers so failure of one control does not remove all protection.
Fail closed
Block the protected action when a required safety or authorization check cannot complete.
Indirect prompt injection
Adversarial instructions hidden in external content such as pages, documents, email, or tool results.
Excessive agency
More autonomy or capability than is necessary for the intended task.
Pre-action approval
Human authorization before a consequential action occurs.
Sampled review
Reviewing a subset of lower-risk cases to monitor quality and drift.
Control evidence
Records/artifacts demonstrating that a required control is implemented and operating.
Compliance boundary
The systems, data, services, and responsibilities included in the regulated/authorized scope.
Fairness evaluation
Assessing relevant performance/outcomes across appropriate groups or slices instead of relying only on aggregate metrics.
Accountability
Clear ownership for architecture decisions, residual risk, monitoring, and incident response.
Hard safety properties should be enforced by {{c1::controls at the relevant system boundary}}, not only by prompt text.
High-risk authorization checks often should {{c1::fail closed}} when verification is unavailable.
Agent safety benefits from {{c1::defense in depth}} across model, tool, environment, and human controls.
External content consumed by an agent should be treated as {{c1::untrusted}} because it may contain indirect prompt injection.
Reducing unnecessary tools and credentials limits the {{c1::blast radius}} of excessive agency.
Human oversight should scale with {{c1::consequence and reversibility}}, not merely model confidence.
A reviewer needs enough {{c1::evidence and policy context}} to make a meaningful decision.
A useful compliance mapping is requirement → control → owner → {{c1::evidence}} → review cadence.
A vendor's compliance status does not automatically make the {{c1::entire application}} compliant.
Responsible AI requires clear {{c1::accountability}} rather than saying “the AI decided.”
Transparency does not require exposing private {{c1::chain-of-thought}}.
What security design uses several independent protective layers?
Defense in depth
What failure behavior blocks an action when a required control cannot verify it?
Fail closed
What attack embeds malicious instructions in content the agent reads?
Indirect prompt injection
What risk describes granting an agent more autonomy or permissions than required?
Excessive agency
What review pattern requires human authorization before execution?
Pre-action approval
What review pattern checks only a fraction of lower-risk cases?
Sampled review
What term describes records proving a control is implemented and operating?
Control evidence
What concept means a named person/team owns residual risk and response?
Accountability
A refund tool can transfer money. The system prompt says “never refund more than $500,” but the API accepts any amount. What is the strongest improvement?

[{"id":"a","text":"Enforce the limit in deterministic transaction/authorization logic before execution."},{"id":"b","text":"Repeat the warning five times in the prompt."},{"id":"c","text":"Use a more persuasive role description."},{"id":"d","text":"Log over-$500 refunds after they happen."}]

An agent has production write access even though its task is read-only analysis. Which risk is most direct?

What is the architect's first job during discovery?
Translate ambiguous stakeholder language into testable outcomes, constraints, and requirements.
Why should adjectives such as “fast” or “accurate” be converted into numbers/tests?
So architecture and acceptance can be evaluated objectively.
What ownership questions belong in discovery?
Who approves requirements, owns residual risk, and supports the system in production.
What makes an architecture recommendation useful?
It explains why the chosen option fits the constraints and what trade-offs it accepts.
Why adapt architecture communication by audience?
Different stakeholders need different implications and evidence while the underlying decision remains consistent.
What should accompany a recommendation besides benefits?
Costs, risks, alternatives, reversibility, and supporting evidence.
Why should stakeholders receive measurable expectations for AI systems?
Probabilistic systems cannot responsibly be described with promises of perfect behavior.
What makes a feedback loop actionable?
A signal, trigger/threshold, owner, investigation process, action, and verification.
When should a team re-architect instead of merely iterate?
When a fundamental constraint changed or the architecture pattern itself is the bottleneck.
What should architecture documentation preserve besides diagrams?
Decision context, constraints, alternatives, rationale, assumptions, ownership, and review triggers.
What is the purpose of an ADR?
Record a significant architecture decision and the context/trade-offs behind it.
What lifecycle phases are explicitly in the CCAR-P objective?
Discovery, design, handoff, monitoring, and iteration.
Why cannot monitoring compensate for missing discovery?
You cannot monitor success reliably if requirements and acceptance criteria were never defined.
Functional requirement
What the solution must do.
Non-functional requirement
How the solution must operate, such as latency, availability, scale, residency, or cost.
Trade-off
A deliberate exchange where improving one property costs or constrains another.
Reversibility
How easily and cheaply an architecture decision can be changed later.
Feedback signal
Observed evidence such as user reports, tool errors, cost drift, or safety incidents.
SLA
An agreed service-level expectation/commitment for measurable service behavior.
ADR
Architecture Decision Record documenting a significant decision, context, alternatives, and rationale.
Runbook
Operational guidance for diagnosing, responding to, and recovering from known conditions/incidents.
Handoff
Transition from architecture/design into implementation and operational ownership with acceptance criteria and guidance.
Iteration
Evidence-driven changes after design/launch, accompanied by updated evaluation and documentation.
Discovery should turn vague goals into {{c1::observable acceptance criteria}} before design.
A stakeholder's proposed implementation is not the same as the underlying {{c1::requirement}}.
Unresolved assumptions should have a named {{c1::owner}} rather than remaining implicit.
A strong recommendation explains {{c1::why the option fits the constraints}}, not just what components it uses.
Architecture communication should expose meaningful {{c1::trade-offs}} rather than hiding concessions.
A useful feedback loop has a signal, trigger, owner, action, and {{c1::verification}}.
A user thumbs-down is a {{c1::signal}}, not by itself a complete root-cause evaluation.
An architecture diagram without {{c1::decision rationale}} is incomplete for long-term handoff.
Document decisions that are expensive, risky, or {{c1::hard to reverse}}.
The CCAR-P lifecycle is discovery → design → handoff → monitoring → {{c1::iteration}}.
Handoff is incomplete without explicit {{c1::ownership and acceptance criteria}}.
What requirement category describes what the system must do?
Functional requirement
What requirement category covers latency, availability, scale, and cost?
Non-functional requirement
What term describes the cost/ease of changing an architecture decision later?
Reversibility
What term describes exchanging one architecture benefit for another cost or constraint?
Trade-off
What agreement sets measurable service expectations such as latency or availability?
SLA
What should happen after a feedback-driven change to confirm it worked?
Verification

What is the key distinction between an instruction and a control?
An instruction influences model behavior; a control enforces what the runtime is permitted to do.
Why should team-level Claude configuration be standardized?
Shared guidance, tools, permissions, and Skills reduce inconsistent behavior and operational drift.
What should AI-assisted development optimize?
Developer throughput while preserving independent verification, security boundaries, and human accountability.
How should verification strength change with consequence?
More consequential changes require stronger independent tests, review, and approval.
What is the core operational debugging loop?
Move from symptom to evidence to likely layer to fix to verification.
Why should a runbook include rollback/fallback and an owner?
Operators need safe recovery actions and clear escalation responsibility during incidents.
Instruction
Guidance intended to influence model behavior.
Runtime control
An enforceable runtime, permission, sandbox, policy, or CI boundary.
Verification tool
An independent mechanism such as tests, linters, type checks, security scans, or CI used to check generated changes.
Reviewability
The ability for developers to understand and own an AI-generated change.
Operational runbook
Documented operational steps for diagnosis, mitigation, rollback/fallback, escalation, and evidence preservation.
“Do not modify production” is an instruction; removing production credentials is an enforceable {{c1::control}}.
Shared Skills and configuration should be {{c1::versioned and reviewed}} like other operational assets.
AI assistance should accelerate the engineering loop, not bypass {{c1::CI, code review, or security boundaries}}.
